label: Threads
terms_note: Free; Meta app with the Threads use case; scopes threads_basic (all), threads_content_publish, threads_manage_replies, threads_read_replies, threads_manage_insights (+ keyword search / delete / mentions per the reference); each permission needs App Review and a published app before non-tester users can authorize; 250 published posts per 24 h; 500-character text; long-lived tokens last 60 days and refresh via GET /refresh_access_token. Caution (docs read 2026-09-24): 'If your app has not been approved for advanced access for the threads_manage_mentions permission, the API returns only mentions made by a Threads tester on the app' (https://developers.facebook.com/docs/threads/threads-mentions); every Threads permission beyond testers goes through Meta App Review.

tools.name: publish_image
tools.endpoint: same container flow with media_type=IMAGE / CAROUSEL

tools.name: publish_video
tools.endpoint: same container flow with media_type=VIDEO (poll the container status first)

auth: 1. Meta app with the **Threads use case** (its own app id / secret).
2. Authorization Window → code (1 h) → short-lived token (1 h) → `GET /access_token?grant_type=th_exchange_token` →
4. Each permission must pass App Review and the app must be published before non-tester users can authorize.

endpoints.purpose: views, likes, replies, reposts, quotes, followers

reference.limits: - 250 published posts per 24 h; 500-character text; carousels 2–20 items; ≤ 5 unique URLs per text post. - Free; Meta Platform Terms; long-lived token must be refreshed before day 60. - No scheduling parameter — platform-side scheduler.

fields.name: access_token
fields.help: Threads user access token (long-lived, 60 days; refresh with GET /refresh_access_token) of the Threads profile, from an app with the Threads use case; scopes threads_basic, threads_content_publish, threads_read_replies, threads_manage_replies, threads_manage_mentions, threads_manage_insights, threads_delete. Sent as the access_token query parameter, as every Threads example does (https://developers.facebook.com/docs/threads/posts).

me.note: GET /me?fields=id,username,name,threads_biography,is_verified ('You may only fetch the profile of the app-scoped user').

publish_text.note: One call: POST /me/threads with media_type=TEXT and auto_publish_text=true - 'When this optional flag is passed, a Threads post is published automatically when a Threads media container is created without needing to go through the extra publish step. Note: This only works for text posts.' `reply_to` is sent as reply_to_id. Text posts are limited to 500 characters; 250 published posts per 24 h.

read_comments.note: GET /{threads_media_id}/replies 'only returns the top-level replies' (reverse chronological by default); nested replies need /conversation. `username` 'only works for public users and your own user'. Cursor paging: page/limit are not sent.

reply_comment.note: A reply is a text post with reply_to_id ('Required if replying to a post') published in one call with auto_publish_text=true.

read_mentions.note: GET /me/mentions: 'public Threads media objects in which a Threads profile has been tagged by another Threads profile' (threads_manage_mentions). `since` is not sent (the API takes a Unix timestamp >= 1688540400, not ISO-8601); cursor paging, so page/limit are not sent.

delete.note: DELETE /{threads_media_id} (threads_delete) answers {success: true, deleted_id}. 'The Delete endpoint has a rate limit of 100 deletes per day per account.'

analytics_post.note: GET /{threads_media_id}/insights?metric=likes,replies,reposts,quotes,views,shares returns data[] entries {name, period: lifetime, values[{value}], id: '<media_id>/insights/<metric>/lifetime'}; the documented example answers in the requested order, which the positional mapping relies on - check raw.data[].name. `post_id` is the first entry's id ('<media_id>/insights/likes/lifetime'). 'An empty array will be returned for REPOST_FACADE posts'. views and shares are 'in development'.

not_offered.publish_image: Image posts take two calls: 'Create a media container ... using the POST /{threads-user-id}/threads endpoint' then 'Publish the media container using the POST /{threads-user-id}/threads_publish endpoint' (https://developers.facebook.com/docs/threads/posts); auto_publish_text 'only works for text posts' (https://developers.facebook.com/docs/threads/reference/publishing).

evidence: host graph.threads.com: DNS ok, TLSv1.3 (DigiCert Inc)
probe: 7/7 tools answered on their documented path with an auth refusal, a validation error or data; control route answered 400 too, so the host authenticates before routing
